programme: TP53 and HMGA2 form the genome-/chromatin-instability core (HMGA2 is a canonical antagonist of p53-driven target activation via chromatin competition), MBD1 sits on the epigenetic-silencing layer over that instability (methyl-CpG-binding repression of immune/DNA-damage-linked loci, including IRF8 and IFNG among its own targets), and IRF2/IRF7 run the interferon-stimulated-gene output that this kind of instability classically triggers (IRF7 as the inducible activator, IRF2 as its constitutive repressor of the same target class) — with VDR acting as the nuclear-receptor throttle on that interferon/inflammatory output.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease this axis is expected to run as: DNA-damage/chromatin dysregulation (TP53, HMGA2) and epigenetic silencing (MBD1) accompanying neuronal stress, feeding a low-grade interferon/inflammatory output (IRF2/IRF7-class signaling) that VDR modulates — consistent with the retrieved TP53 hub-gene, HMGA2/miR-132/PI3K-AKT, MBD1-neurotoxicity, and VDR-neuroprotection papers, though none of these papers explicitly link the module's pieces to each other within AD.
role_in_b: In rectal/colorectal cancer the same core is a documented instability-and-immune-evasion module: TP53 mutation drives clonal evolution, HMGA2 overexpression drives EMT/stemness and chemoresistance, and IRF2/IRF7-class interferon signaling shapes antitumor immunity and prognosis — each independently supported by the retrieved CRC papers; VDR's role is comparatively weak here, since the retrieved VDR-CRC papers mostly report null polymorphism associations.
shared_axis: Both diseases involve age- and damage-associated genomic/epigenetic instability (TP53, HMGA2, MBD1) that can chronically engage the same interferon-response circuitry (IRF2, IRF7), with VDR as a plausible tuning input on that response in postmitotic neurons in one disease and in proliferating epithelium in the other — a shared instability-to-inflammation logic rather than a shared cell type or tissue.
reasoning: No retrieved paper states an AD-rectal cancer connection through this module; instead, TP53 and HMGA2 are separately documented in AD and, more strongly, in CRC, and IRF2/IRF7 are documented in CRC but only inferred for AD from Open Targets percentile rather than direct papers. The module is nameable from real functional relationships among the six factors (p53/HMGA2 antagonism, IRF7/IRF2 as an activator-repressor pair, MBD1 silencing immune loci), but the cross-disease link rests on reasoning about a shared damage/inflammation logic, not on retrieved evidence tying the two diseases together — hence moderate, not strong.
support: PMID 41335161, 41910814, 39112893 (VDR in AD models/patients); PMID 39451780, 36946647, 39201651 (VDR polymorphisms in colorectal cancer, largely null associations); PMID 34150043 (HMGA2 via miR-132/PI3K-AKT in AD mouse model); PMID 38058548, 33986248, 21252160, 26244988 (HMGA2 driving chemoresistance, metastasis, and stemness in colorectal cancer); PMID 42353021 (TP53 as a multi-target hub in AD, jointly with T2DM, not rectal cancer); PMID 42633600 (TP53 mutation in clonal evolution of recurrent rectal cancer); PMID 21859832, 34488791 (interferon-regulatory-factor signaling and colorectal cancer risk/prognosis, IRF2/IRF7 not individually confirmed); PMID 33174148 (MBD1 expression in an AD neurotoxicity mouse model).
how_to_falsify: In a neuronal model of AD-relevant stress and a rectal/colorectal cancer cell line, knock down HMGA2 and MBD1 in parallel and measure p53 target-gene activation (e.g. CDKN1A) and IRF7-driven ISG induction (e.g. ISG15, CXCL10). If HMGA2/MBD1 loss fails to change p53 activity or IRF7-dependent ISG output concordantly in both systems, the proposed instability-to-interferon linkage connecting the two diseases does not hold.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain vs. colorectal epithelium with no anatomical or clinical overlap, so the account rests entirely on a proposed shared molecular logic, not shared physiology. Support fractions (74-112 of 160 comparisons) mean even the top factors are discordant in a substantial minority of patient groups, and this is drawn from only 9 independent cohort pairs. Five of the twelve listed factors (HOXB3, ZBTB18, NR2F6, PAX9, KAT6A) have no literature evidence at all and were deliberately left out of the module rather than folded in. The VDR-CRC papers retrieved mostly report negative/null polymorphism findings, which weakens rather than strengthens VDR's place in the cancer side. Excluded single-view factors (PAX3, HIVEP3, KLF12, MLXIP, TLE5, ESRRG, HOXD10, IRX4) and tissue-generic factors (including EMT/immune master regulators NOTCH1, ZEB1, STAT4) were not used to build this account, per the exclusion lists.
